U06-SRC-NEGATIVE-COMMAND.original_identifier: §156h, §159a continuation; Reader XII p183 editorial line7 (printed margin5/10 nearby)
U06-SRC-NEGATIVE-COMMAND.exact_example: ne ondrǣd ðū ðē ǣniges ðinges
U06-SRC-NEGATIVE-COMMAND.claim: Direct negative second-singular command, spoken by the king to his daughter: ne precedes the imperative ondrǣd. The same words are quoted in the syntax. It does not teach ondrǣdan or its reflexive/genitive frame.

U06-SRC-WITAN-ACCUSATIVE.original_identifier: Reader XII, printed line5 and editorial lines13–14 (printed margins5,10,15)
exact_examples: ðū woldest witan his naman and his gelimp
U06-SRC-WITAN-ACCUSATIVE.claim: Witan in know takes an ordinary accusative nominal object denoting knowledge: noble birth, name, circumstances. Mīne with feminine æðelborennesse confirms accusative rather than a guessed dative; his gelimp is the coordinated neuter accusative object. Supports the declared new composition Ic wāt ðā ðing with those things understood as already mentioned facts/matters. No finite content clause is needed.
U06-SRC-WITAN-ACCUSATIVE.verification: Retained source page visually inspected; lexical government checked independently of mere paradigm or dictionary gloss.
U06-SRC-WITAN-ACCUSATIVE.teaching_boundary: Source nominal objects and surrounding conditional/content syntax are evidence only, not learner assignments or new lexical requirements.
